codeReview.summary: The App Setup feature is largely complete and aligned with the architecture: all six settings routes (settings.tsx, settings._index.tsx, settings.tables.tsx, settings.services.tsx, settings.special-days.tsx, settings.floor-plan.tsx) await requireReservationsAccess first and return null, the browser-direct setup client mints a short-lived setup token (token.ts, scope=setup, read or update grant) and talks to the regional tenant-api with the correct payloads (expectedFloorPlanVersion, expectedVersion aliases accepted by packages/reservations/src/schemas/setup.ts and apps/tenant-api), 409 stale-version handling exists on the settings, tables/services/special-days and floor-plan paths, read-only operators get canWrite=false gating (disabled or hidden controls in every tab), the location settings page renders the Reservations card + deep link and notifies reservations context changes, the floor-plan canvas implements 10-unit grid snap drag, resize, rotation presets, keyboard nudge (+1 / Shift+10) with aria-live announcements, decor elements and dir=ltr geometry under Arabic RTL, and guard/unit/E2E coverage exists (reservations-guards.test.ts, setup-api.test.ts, floor-plan-canvas.test.tsx, tests/e2e/reservations-setup.test.ts, which the worker ran 12/12 with --retries=0 --repeat-each=3). Two blocking defects remain: the floor-plan canvas clears its dirty flag (and renders the 'Saved' badge) after a failed save, which silently loses the local draft, and several user-visible control labels (weekday chips, shape/element option labels, special-day mode and block reason badges) are hardcoded English, violating the mission's 'every user-visible string goes through Lingui' rule and VAL-SETUP-031. The read-only E2E assertion is also vacuous, so read-only gating of the General tab is not actually verified.

issues.description: The floor-plan draft is marked clean (and the UI reports 'Saved') after a FAILED save, which can silently discard the operator's local draft. handleSaveClick awaits onSave(...) (line 588) and then calls setDirty(false) at line 625 unconditionally, but the route's handler swallows every failure: settings.floor-plan.tsx:95-109 catches the 409 conflict (sets conflictMessage) and all other errors (sets errorMessage) and resolves normally, so the canvas cannot tell success from failure. Failure path: (1) an operator drags tables, clicks Save, and the tenant-api answers 409 stale_version or a 5xx; (2) the header badge switches from 'Unsaved draft changes' to 'Saved' (floor-plan-canvas.tsx:654-665), the Discard draft button disappears (683) and Leave no longer asks for confirmation (375-381); (3) the 409 banner instructs the operator to 'inspect your draft before re-applying' and offers 'Reload latest floor plan' (floor-plan-canvas.tsx:770-779 -> settings.floor-plan.tsx:112-116 -> loadFloorPlan), and because dirty is already false the baseline-sync effect (floor-plan-canvas.tsx:152-170) replaces the local draft with server data on the next props change, destroying the edits without any warning. This breaks the feature's required 'local draft with explicit Save and Leave-without-saving discard' semantics. The E2E floor-plan test does not catch it because it saves again without reloading after the 409.

User-visible control labels remain hardcoded English, violating the mission rule 'i18n: every user-visible string goes through Lingui' (mission AGENTS.md:60) and VAL-SETUP-031, which requires Arabic for all navigation tabs, headings, form labels and buttons. Affected: (a) service weekday chip buttons render day.shortLabel ('Sun'...'Sat') from the untranslated WEEKDAY_OPTIONS table (settings.services.tsx:642-655; table at app/utils/reservations/setup-api.ts:340-352) and the service summary returns 'Every day' plus the same English short labels (settings.services.tsx:81-87); (b) the Tables tab shape select renders English option labels from SHAPE_OPTIONS (settings.tables.tsx:60-66 rendered at 865-868); (c) the floor-plan canvas renders English option labels for element kind (ELEMENT_KINDS, floor-plan-canvas.tsx:82-95 rendered at 867-871) and table shape (TABLE_SHAPES, 73-80 rendered at 1155); (d) the Special Days tab prints the raw enum as a badge, sd.kind (settings.special-days.tsx:748) and blk.reason (1021). These strings are literals, not Lingui messages, so npm run lingui:extract / node scripts/check-lingui.mjs cannot see them and the worker's green catalog check does not cover them; they stay English under ?lng=ar.

The read-only assertion is vacuous, so read-only gating of the General tab is not verified. The spec asserts await expect(page.getByTestId('setup-save-general-button')).toHaveCount(0), but the implementation always renders that button for a read-only operator and only disables it (settings._index.tsx:750-762, disabled={!canWrite || saving}, form rendered whenever draft is non-null at 236). toHaveCount(0) resolves as soon as the count is 0, and immediately after navigate the index route still shows the loading card (settings._index.tsx:155-163, loadingSummary && !draft), so the assertion passes before settings load. It is also a race: if the stubbed settings response lands first the count is 1 and the test fails, which is why this assertion should be replaced by an assertion on the loaded state plus the disabled button (as the floor-plan tab already does at line 823).

The floor-plan editor is not a full-screen editor: it renders as a bordered in-page card (min-h-[720px], line 630) inside the reservations settings shell with the sub-tab chrome above it (settings.tsx:289-428), whereas the feature description says 'full-screen floor-plan editor' and the project precedent for full-screen editors is an overlay with an explicit Save and obvious exit (library/app-ui-patterns.md:131-133, email-design-overlay.tsx). Functionally the draft/Save/Leave semantics are present; this is a layout/convention mismatch rather than a broken behavior.

Canvas item aria-labels bypass Lingui: line 971 (`Element ${el.label || el.kind} (${el.x}, ${el.y})`) and line 1041 (`Table ${table.label}, ${table.minCovers}-${table.maxCovers} covers at (${table.x}, ${table.y})`) are raw template strings while the sibling labels at 813, 859, 897 and 918 use _(msg`...`). Screen-reader output for Arabic operators is therefore English-framed (same class of gap as the blocking i18n issue, lower impact because it is assistive text).

Drag sessions are bound to the canvas surface only: startPointerDrag (485-512) records the session and handleCanvasPointerMove (514-570) / handleCanvasPointerUp (572-574) are canvas handlers with no pointer capture and no window-level listeners. Dragging an item past the canvas edge (or releasing the pointer outside it) stalls the item until the pointer re-enters the canvas, and a pointerup outside leaves the stale session in dragRef so the next pointermove over the canvas resumes moving the previously selected item. Minor robustness issue; not covered by the component tests.

sharedStateObservations.observation: library/app-ui-patterns.md:131-133 defines the 'full-screen editors are drafts with an explicit Save and an obvious exit' convention with the email-design-overlay precedent, but the floor-plan editor implements the same draft discipline as an in-page card in the settings shell. Either the doc should say 'dedicated route page with a local draft and explicit Save' or the editor should become an overlay; recording which one the mission wants avoids later workers copying the wrong shape (the next reservations UI features add more editors).

sharedStateObservations.observation: check-lingui.mjs only validates strings that are Lingui messages, so constant label tables, option labels, enum badges and aria-labels stay English and the check still exits 0. The app-ui-worker skill (and/or the i18n section of library/app-ui-patterns.md) should tell workers to grep the routes they touched for string literals in label/option tables and for template-string aria-labels before declaring Arabic complete, because 'npm run lingui:extract && node scripts/check-lingui.mjs' passing is not evidence that every user-visible string is localized.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The Playwright spec was written against assumed test ids and one assertion is vacuous, yet the final run reported 12/12. Three test ids in the first draft did not exist in the implementation (setup-general-save-button, location-reservations-status-card, floor-plan-leave-confirm) and the read-only test now asserts toHaveCount(0) on a control the app renders (disabled) once data loads, passing only during the loading state. The E2E guidance in library/app-ui-patterns.md:256-261 should add: grep the implementation for data-testid before writing the spec, and for absence assertions wait for a loaded marker (or assert the disabled state) instead of relying on toHaveCount(0).

summary: Review of foh-setup-ui (commit d6dd3084, repo /home/factory-user/repos/menuza) against VAL-SETUP-001/002/023-028/031/032 and VAL-CROSS-001: the setup routes, guards, browser-direct token flow, CRUD flows, 409 handling, read-only gating, location-settings Reservations card, Arabic RTL chrome with an LTR canvas, and the E2E/unit/guard suites are all in place and the recorded E2E run passes 12/12 with --retries=0. Two blocking defects: (1) floor-plan-canvas.tsx:625 clears dirty after a failed save, so a 409/5xx shows 'Saved', drops the Leave guard and lets the next 'Reload latest floor plan' silently replace the unsaved draft; (2) several user-visible labels (weekday chips, shape and element-kind option labels, special-day mode and block reason badges) are hardcoded English and never extracted, violating the mission i18n rule and VAL-SETUP-031. Non-blocking: the read-only E2E assertion passes vacuously during loading and does not verify General-tab gating; the editor is not literally full-screen; two canvas aria-labels are untranslated; drags are not pointer-captured. Shared-state notes cover the full-screen-editor convention, the check-lingui blind spot for hardcoded strings, and E2E testid/absence-assertion guidance.
